clue.text: Firemen do get lost!

definitions.meaning: what fire crews do when called out: head for the fires
a rude dismissal, telling someone to clear off

explanation.definitionFit: Firefighters travel to fires, and the same phrase is an old-fashioned curse meaning 'clear off'.

clue.text: Good publicity in Rialto, perhaps, for movie

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other, here the advert set into the shuffled place name
perhaps suggests the letters of Rialto are one possible arrangement among others

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A film is promoted with posters around the Rialto in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rialto is a Venice bridge, which the surface leans on; 'perhaps' makes LIATOR and 'in' splits it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiator is a 2000 Ridley Scott film, so the clue's movie is one example.

clue.text: Smart upholstery for car

definitions.meaning: neat and well turned out, as an adjective
the interior finishing and fittings of a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A tidy person looks neat; motor makers call seat covers and interior finish the vehicle's trim.

clue.text: Guard releases female bird

indicators.note: releases means the guard lets go of one letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder guarding the Tower of London

explanation.surface: A guard frees a female prisoner, in a scene at the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London. 'releases' removes F from BEEFEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches flying insects.

clue.text: Cockney injured, carrying guns

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker of East London drops the initial aitch, so the H goes

parts.note: to be injured is to be harmed

explanation.surface: An East Ender who was hurt is now going about with weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class dialect of East London, famous for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bearing weapons, such as pistols, is described as armed.

clue.text: Distinguished female artist went topless

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist known for her unmade bed

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, which is its first letter in an across-style reading

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A distinguished woman artist went about without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the W of WENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished figure is renowned and well respected in their field.

clue.text: Bet it's the wife

parts.note: taking half of the word better leaves its first three letters, which spell this clue word

explanation.surface: A gambler admits that the wager was his wife's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, 'half of better', gives BET, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's spouse is affectionately called his better half.

clue.text: Girl: see one entering America

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: entering says one goes into the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Look at this girl newly arrived in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sets the numeral after the first letter of the country's abbreviation, giving UISA.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa is a female given name, as in the author Louisa May Alcott.

clue.text: Musical fellow makes comeback, reviving memories of the past

indicators.note: a comeback turns the whole pair of words round so they read back to front

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical about Eva Peron
cove is old British slang for a chap

explanation.surface: A musical man returns to the stage, stirring nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes comeback' reverses EVITA + COVE as a whole, giving EVOC + ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up feelings and images from earlier times.

clue.text: Letters chap read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the word for a man is heard, not seen, and spelt differently

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A man reads his letters out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Post delivered to a house is a collection of letters and parcels.

clue.text: Rita recollected about four pieces of useless information

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged name around the numeral
recollected read as re-collected says the letters of the name are gathered in a new order

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Rita remembers some pointless facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' gives TRIA, and 'about' wraps that round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are minor facts of little importance, the stuff of pub quizzes.

clue.text: Doctor may dread idle fantasy

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician might fear a patient's wishful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning tamper with; it rearranges MAY DREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant reverie indulged in while awake.

clue.text: Officer at main prison

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer
the main is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: An officer is stationed at the city's main jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious prison in Southwark, London, where Dickens's father was held for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a historic debtors' jail on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Gives response regarding book

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone replies to a letter about a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something that happens.

clue.text: One trying to lap American driver

indicators.note: to lap is to wrap round, so the tester encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a tester is someone who tries things out

explanation.surface: A racer tries to lap a rival American driver on the circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap' is a racing word in the surface; here it means wrap round, splitting the tester after TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teamster is a lorry driver in the US, originally one who drove a team of horses.

clue.text: Loyal servant, firm and organised? Yes

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Asked whether a loyal servant is efficient and orderly, the answer is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' gives MANFRID from the two words; the question mark and 'Yes' supply the old affirmative at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Friday is the faithful helper of Robinson Crusoe, hence any devoted assistant.

clue.text: Elegant expression is Greek to me

parts.note: Attic is the dialect of ancient Athens, so Greek
M is the initial of me, an occasional crossword shortening

explanation.surface: A stylish turn of phrase is incomprehensible to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the idiom 'it's all Greek to me', meaning unintelligible.
explanation.definitionFit: An Atticism is a refined phrase in the polished Athenian style.

clue.text: Precise account by clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant priest in a parish

explanation.surface: A vicar's assistant gives an exact report.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and correct work is free from error.

clue.text: A hundred or so can be seen on a Mediterranean island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
sic is Latin for thus or so, used to flag a quoted error

explanation.surface: Around a hundred people may be spotted on a sunny island.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A that opens the clue is only an article; the A in the answer comes from 'a' before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island off the west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Robbery succeeded, of course

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded in genealogical tables
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A robbery worked, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a quick grab, as in a bag theft or a smash-and-grab raid.

clue.text: Polynesian article supporting secret society

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article backs a hidden organisation in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts AN under TONG in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongans come from Tonga, an island kingdom of Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: In emergency situation, help to make tree steady

parts.note: the fir is a conifer
staid means sober and steady

explanation.surface: Advice to prop up a falling tree in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic medical care given at the scene of an accident before professionals arrive.

clue.text: Convoluted plot involving old Jewish actor

indicators.note: involving means holding within, so the twisted letters enclose the abbreviation
convoluted means twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tangled storyline features an elderly Jewish performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convoluted' rearranges PLOT into TOPL, and 'involving' wraps it round O. Chaim Topol was the Israeli star of Fiddler on the Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaim Topol was an Israeli film and stage performer, famous as Tevye.

clue.text: Belgian who sang about a French engineer

indicators.note: about puts the singer's name around the French word

parts.note: Jacques Brel was a Belgian singer-songwriter
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Belgian singer performed a song about a French engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian British engineer of railways and ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel built the Great Western Railway and the steamship Great Britain.

clue.text: Some lonesome nights — a sign of what's to come

definitions.text: a sign of what's to come

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few lonely nights may be a warning of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign foretelling a future event, good or bad.

clue.text: One who's ineffective with naughty child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A feeble person is saddled with a badly behaved youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakling lacks courage or force; a feeble person.

clue.text: I'm to act as go-between without delay

parts.note: to mediate is to negotiate between two parties

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to step in at once as a negotiator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at once happens instantly, straight away.

clue.text: Flipping coins somewhere in County Antrim

parts.note: flipping and bally are both mild British intensifiers, euphemisms for stronger swear words
coins are money

explanation.surface: Tossing coins at a place in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like tossing a coin but is the mild oath BALLY. Ballymoney is a town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballymoney is a town in the north of Northern Ireland.
